chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, from Aban, from Abu al-Udais who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Salih! Follow the one who makes you weep and he is a sincere adviser to you, and do not follow the one who makes you laugh and he is a deceiver to you. And you will all return before God and then you will know.'

key_terms.غَاشّ: A deceiver, one who conceals their true malicious intent behind outward pleasantness
key_terms.نَاصِح: A sincere counsellor or adviser who wishes genuine good for another; opposite of a flatterer
key_terms.يُبْكِيكَ: Makes you weep — referring to the grief that comes from honest and sincere advice
key_terms.يُضْحِكُكَ: Makes you laugh — referring to the false ease and flattery of a deceitful companion

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about choosing sincere companions over flatterers?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) addresses a companion named Salih, delivering a profound teaching on choosing companions and spiritual mentors. The Imam contrasts two types of people: one whose sincere counsel may cause grief but stems from genuine care, and another whose flattery brings laughter but conceals deception and betrayal. This wisdom reflects the early Islamic emphasis on the importance of righteous companionship (suhba) as a means of spiritual purification, with the reminder that all will face divine accountability.
